description: Replace the integrated n512 path's multi-launch 16-column panel and ATen trailing-update sequence with a persistent clustered reducer that retains XOR-swizzled row-warp staging, forms exact reflectors across CTAs, consumes compact V/W in direct tcgen05 or WMMA symmetric rank updates, and emits panel-ready reflectors without concatenation or Python dispatch; preserve fused solve, prefix reconstruction, certificates, stress routing, CUDA guards, and every other size.

Replaced the n512 Python 32-panel loop, concatenations, and ATen trailing updates with one four-CTA persistent cluster. All CTAs cooperatively form exact Householder vectors in DSM, retain V/W across the panel, emit direct reflectors, and apply each symmetric rank-32 update with in-kernel TF32 WMMA plus FP32 edge tiles. All 39 validations pass, but the persistent kernel costs 67.750 ms versus about 44.9 ms for the parent panel+update sequence; dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 are 120318/166506/300810 us and full metric is 38342.277 us.

Attempted a DSM TF32x3 update by splitting every completed V/W panel into TF32 high and residual components, then issuing high-high, high-low, and low-high MMA terms for each symmetric product. CUDA 13.3 exposes the conversion helper only in an internal namespace on this compile path, so nvcc rejected the unqualified __float_to_tf32 identifier; no validation or metric was produced.

Implemented direct TF32x3 symmetric updates inside the persistent cluster: completed V/W panels are split across DSM ranks into TF32 high and residual components, and each product accumulates high-high, high-low, and low-high MMA terms. All 39 validations pass and LAPACK-even n512 improves from the one-pass trial 300810 to 129391 us by avoiding bulk repair, but six MMA terms raise the persistent reducer from 67.750 to 106.255 ms; dense/mixed are 156331/182899 us and full metric is 36935.407 us.

Transposed completed TF32 high/residual V/W panels into contiguous row-major 16-wide DSM tiles on dedicated ranks so WMMA consumes A row-major and B column-major with leading dimension 16 instead of conflict-heavy column-major stride 512. All 39 validations pass, but remote-rank WMMA load latency exceeds the bank-conflict savings: dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 are 172111/194323/145842 us and full metric regresses to 37717.803 us.

Replaced the persistent WMMA path with 32 four-CTA clustered Householder panels driven entirely from C++, writing direct [W,V,W] triplets for one rank-32 ATen tensor-core update per panel and eliminating Python dispatch and concatenation. All 39 validations pass; dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 are 110010/150214/83084 us and full metric is 34233.512 us. Exact profile shows clustered panel formation costs 53.830 ms versus the parent one-CTA panels about 30.47 ms, while library updates retain about 14.3 ms.

Reduced n512 panel clusters from four 384-thread CTAs to two 512-thread CTAs, retaining 1024 cooperative threads while halving DSM participants and cluster barriers. All 39 validations pass. Dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 improve to 93759/137021/67476 us and full metric to 33032.326 us. Exact profile shows clustered panels fall from 53.830 to 38.262 ms, still above the parent one-CTA 30.47 ms; library updates remain about 13.8 ms.

Reduced the two-CTA n512 panel cluster to 256 threads per CTA, matching the parent 512-thread total while retaining DSM formation, C++ dispatch, and direct triplet updates. All 39 validations pass, but lower row-dot service dominates the reduced barrier footprint: dense/mixed/LAPACK-even are 105035/144104/77794 us and full metric regresses to 33820.339 us versus 33032.326 for two 512-thread CTAs.

Widened the two-CTA n512 cluster to 768 threads per rank, matching the four-rank trial total of 1536 cooperative threads while keeping only two DSM participants. All 39 validations pass. Dense/mixed/LAPACK-even are 103226/142789/76296 us and full metric is 33706.297 us; this is faster than two 256-thread ranks but slower than the selected two 512-thread geometry at 33032.326.

Tested two 640-thread n512 panel ranks, supplying 1280 cluster threads with the B200-oriented geometry used by the larger reducer. All 39 validations pass. Dense/mixed/LAPACK-even are 104788/142545/77101 us and full metric is 33787.907 us, leaving two 512-thread ranks as the measured cluster selection.

Collapsed the direct-triplet n512 reducer to one 512-thread cluster rank, eliminating remote DSM exchange while retaining C++ panel dispatch and concatenation-free rank-32 updates. All 39 validations pass. Dense/mixed/LAPACK-even are 90524/134415/63325 us and full metric is 32781.054 us. Exact profile shows panels at 33.911 ms, about 3.44 ms above the selected XOR-swizzled parent, with updates about 14.2 ms.

Specialized the one-rank direct-triplet reducer to local shared pointers, compile-time rank zero, and block barriers in place of DSM mapping and cluster.sync, preserving all panel arithmetic. All 39 validations pass, but dense/mixed/LAPACK-even rise to 95256/136044/68235 us and full metric to 33104.397 us; the size-one cluster primitives were at least as efficient as explicit block specialization.

Retained the selected XOR-swizzled exact-order n512 panel but emitted [W,V,W] directly into one reusable workspace, drove all 32 panels and rank-32 updates inside prefix512, and removed Python panel dispatch plus both concatenations. All 39 validations pass. Full metric is 32498.129 us; dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 are 87234/132043/60030 us versus parent 87506/131967/60466. Exact profile confirms no CatArray kernels and unchanged panel time 25.319+5.194=30.513 ms.

Attempted to fold the final six-column panel two-by-two trailing update into the panel kernel and skip its tiny baddbmm launch. nvcc rejected the in-place write because the shared panel kernel still declared its matrix pointer const from the former out-of-kernel update contract; no validation or metric was produced.

Completed the final-tail fold by making the selected panel matrix contract mutable: the six-column panel now applies its 2x2 trailing update in strict FP32 and C++ skips the last tiny baddbmm launch. All 39 validations pass. New best full metric is 32429.965 us versus parent 32451.361; dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 improve from parent 87506/131967/60466 to 86569/131507/59570 us.

Removed the obsolete standalone sytrd_panel512 declaration, wrapper, allocations, and pybind export so prefix512 is the sole n512 reduction owner. Clean build/kernelguard and all 39 validations pass. Full metric is 32474.274 us, within run noise of selected pre-cleanup 32429.965; dense/mixed/LAPACK-even remain improved at 86715/131565/59978 us versus parent 87506/131967/60466.

Final confirmation of clean direct-triplet n512 integration after obsolete-binding removal. Exact commit builds cleanly, kernelguard is clean, all 39 validations pass, and full metric is 32435.068 us. Dense/mixed/LAPACK-even n512 are 86460/131531/59782 us; exact profile shows panels 25.145+5.194=30.339 ms, no Cat kernels, and no final tiny baddbmm launch.

Selected clean commit 7946df7136921b6f5b1d79dd24a063a00bb61f68. Final build and kernelguard pass, all 39/39 validation/stress cases pass, and confirmation geomean is 32435.068099 us versus parent 32451.360903. N512 dense/mixed/LAPACK-even are 86459.541/131531.459/59781.846 us versus parent integration 87506/131967/60466. The selected source retains the exact XOR-swizzled accurate/fast 16-column panel arithmetic, but prefix512 now owns all 32 panels and rank-32 updates in C++, emits one reusable [W,V,W] workspace directly, removes both Cat kernels and Python panel dispatch, applies the final six-column 2x2 tail update in-kernel, and removes the obsolete standalone pybind path. Exact final profile profiles/2026-07-03-13-39-25/brief-36-trial-14-7946df7136921b6f5b1d79dd24a063a00bb61f68.nsys-rep shows panels 25.145+5.194=30.339 ms, no CatArray kernels, prefix 3.191 ms, and fused solve 3.685 ms. Structural measurements: four-CTA library-update panels cost 53.830 ms/full 34233.512; two 512-thread CTAs cut panels to 38.262 ms/full 33032.326 and beat two 256/640/768-thread variants; one-rank generic panels cost 33.911 ms/full 32781.054. A fully persistent four-CTA direct-WMMA reducer passed 39/39 but cost 67.750 ms and full 38342.277; TF32x3 restored dense-even repair behavior but raised it to 106.255 ms/full 36935.407; row-major DSM operands regressed to 37717.803. Focused NCU on the persistent path measured 0.18 eligible warps/scheduler, 35% scoreboard plus 35% barrier stalls, 44% excessive global sectors, and 28% excessive shared wavefronts. Keep the tree moving: concrete open directions are a tcgen05/TMA warp-specialized update that avoids WMMA/DSM barrier latency, exact-order row-dot loader warps for the 44% sector excess, and fusing several late small panels (not only the final 2x2 tail) while leaving large updates in CUTLASS. This worker made no leaderboard submission and claims no remote score.
